runs.content: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) picked up at the previous close ($160.70) — wide-moat, 5-star-at-flag Morningstar pick with a 22% discount and a Strong Buy analyst consensus (~15% upside to the $185.36 average target), chosen over Clorox (fresh multi-broker downgrades, deteriorating revenue/earnings) and Hershey (already re-rated near its target). Its pending $6B MarketAxess acquisition ties directly into today's dominant headline — a global bond sell-off and the 10-year Treasury yield hitting levels last seen January 2025, compounded by renewed U.S.-Iran Strait of Hormuz tension. F was exited discretionarily (−8.77%, −$88) to keep the book at 35 open positions after ICE's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 34 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,504 (+4.72% on $53,000).

Occidental Petroleum (OXY) picked up at the previous close ($59.10) — pure-play E&P leverage to the weekend US-Iran Strait of Hormuz strikes and resulting oil-price spike (WTI ~$85.46), backed by a standalone Aug 5 beat-and-raise (EPS $2.40 vs. $1.88 est., record production, debt cut $1.5B to $11.8B, 8% dividend increase), chosen over XOM/HAL (less direct crude torque) and VLO (refining margins can compress on a fast crude spike). WMT was exited discretionarily (−7.82%, −$78) to keep the book at 35 open positions after OXY's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 34 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,775 (+5.34% on $52,000).
